# EOM — Eye On Metadata

EOM is a free, open-source, cross-platform desktop application (and command-line tool) that shows what files reveal through their metadata — location, author, device serial numbers, editing history — rates the privacy risk of each file, and removes the sensitive metadata. It runs entirely on the user's machine; no files are uploaded and no account is required.

## Key facts

- Latest version: 2.2.1
- License: MIT
- Website: https://abogo-nono.github.io/eom-eye-on-metadata/
- Source code: https://github.com/abogo-nono/eom
- Download (always the latest release): https://github.com/abogo-nono/eom/releases/latest
- Author: Abogo Lincoln (https://github.com/abogo-nono)
- Platforms: Windows 10+ (x86-64), macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon), Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 20.04+ / glibc 2.31+)
- Interface languages: English, French
- Price: free

## What EOM does

- **Privacy-risk score**: every tag is classified (location, identity, unique IDs and serial numbers, device, dates, software, thumbnails, copyright, technical) and each file is rated High, Medium, Low or Clean from the most sensitive category it contains.
- **Selective cleaning** with profiles: Remove everything, Full anonymity, Social media sharing, Keep copyright, Location only — or hand-picked categories and individual tags. A live preview shows which tags will be removed or kept.
- **Safe by default**: cleaned copies can be written to another folder; EOM asks before modifying originals.
- **Before / after verification**: every cleaned file is read again and compared with the original.
- **Editing**: title, author, copyright, description and date; shift every date by a fixed offset (wrong camera clock); on one file or a whole folder.
- **Export** to JSON, CSV, HTML report or plain text.
- **Preview and map**: image, PDF and Office thumbnails, audio cover art; geotagged files on an OpenStreetMap map (opt-in).
- **Command-line interface**: `eom extract | risk | clean | edit | profiles`.

## Supported formats

- **Images**: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, HEIC/HEIF (HEIC needs ExifTool)
- **Audio**: MP3, FLAC, OGG, Opus, WAV, AIFF, M4A, WMA, APE, WavPack
- **Video**: MP4, M4V, MOV, MKV, WebM
- **Documents**: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX
- **With ExifTool installed**: RAW camera files and hundreds of other formats (read)

## Privacy model

All processing happens locally. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no account. EOM never needs an internet connection. Its only two network features are off by default and must be enabled in Settings: loading map tiles from OpenStreetMap, and checking GitHub for a new release.

## Command line examples

```
eom risk ~/Pictures -r                                   # exit code 0 clean/low, 1 medium, 2 high
eom clean ~/Pictures -r --profile social --output-dir ~/clean
eom extract ~/Documents -r -o report.html
eom edit photo.jpg --author "Jane" --shift +2h
```

## Frequently asked questions

**Does EOM upload my files?**
No. Every operation is performed on your device.

**How do I remove GPS location from a photo?**
Drop the photo (or its folder) on EOM, choose the "Location only" or "Social media sharing" profile and click Clean. The preview shows what will be removed first; cleaned copies can be written to another folder.

**Do I need ExifTool?**
No. EOM uses ExifTool when it is installed and its built-in readers (Pillow, mutagen, pypdf) otherwise. The Windows download bundles ExifTool.

**How is EOM different from online metadata tools?**
Online tools upload your file to a server. EOM processes everything locally, handles whole folders and rates the privacy risk of each file.
